evidence.detail: Input: `/kiwi-wave-master ROADMAP_ITEM=RM-4` with no PRD path; RM-4 has Actual Start '-', Targets '-', Requirements '-'. FR-FLOW-226 AC-1 (docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:15710) requires, 'at the start of the run', a single `update_roadmap_item` call whose link branch depends on 'the work graph's `scope`' (target vs requirement list), and AC-3 (:15712) forbids any other update_roadmap_item call. FR-FLOW-212 AC-1 (:14795) makes the run begin with kiwi-prd, then /kiwi-srs, impact analysis and `wave propose`, and only then commits waves.json, the graph that holds `scope` (50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16382); whether the run narrows to `scope.requirements` is decided at decomposition (FR-FLOW-212 AC-4, :14798). So at the start of the run the object AC-1 branches on does not exist. Taking the call at the first step and linking the product target (the only scope known then) then narrowing to {FR-A, FR-B} reproduces the iter-3 F-3 outcome AC-1's own fills: line (:15704) and Research note (:15735) say it avoids; deferring the call until the graph is committed is not 'the start of the run' under FR-FLOW-212 AC-1, and no second call is allowed by AC-3. FR-FLOW-222 AC-1 (:15439) puts the graph on 'the run's first journal line', which supports the deferred reading, but FR-FLOW-226 does not name that point, so a test cannot decide when the single call must happen.

findings.description: AC-1 makes its single run-start call branch on the work graph's scope, but the run's order (FR-FLOW-212 AC-1) writes that graph, and decides any narrowing, only after kiwi-prd, kiwi-srs and decomposition; the point of the call is undefined.
findings.suggested_action: State the point of the single AC-1 call as the moment the work graph is committed (the run's first journal line, FR-FLOW-222 AC-1), with Actual Start still set to the run's start date.
